# wallix.bastion.cluster

Manage clusters on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.1.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete a cluster on a WALLIX Bastion.
- A cluster groups several targets so that sessions opened on the cluster are spread over them.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_cluster` Terraform resource.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-account-mappings"></a>**account_mappings** | `list / elements=str` | Account mapping targets of the cluster, as `<device>:<service>`. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the account mapping targets of the cluster. Use `[]` to remove them all. |
| <a id="parameter-accounts"></a>**accounts** | `list / elements=str` | Account targets of the cluster, as `<account>@<domain>@<device>:<service>`, for example `administrator@local@srv-win-01:RDP`. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the account targets of the cluster. Use `[]` to remove them all. |
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-cluster-name"></a>**cluster_name** | `str` / required | Name of the cluster. Identifies the cluster on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-description"></a>**description** | `str` | Description of the cluster. |
| <a id="parameter-interactive-logins"></a>**interactive_logins** | `list / elements=str` | Interactive login targets of the cluster, as `<device>:<service>`. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the interactive login targets of the cluster. Use `[]` to remove them all. |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the cluster should exist.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- A cluster needs at least one target in [`accounts`](#parameter-accounts), [`account_mappings`](#parameter-account-mappings) or [`interactive_logins`](#parameter-interactive-logins). The module fails, in check mode too, when the cluster would have none.
- The Bastion 12.4 only accepts targets on RDP services in a cluster.
- The devices, services and accounts referenced must exist; the Bastion rejects the change otherwise.
- The application targets of a cluster (the `applications` field of [`cluster`](#return-cluster)) are returned but not managed, and are kept when the cluster is updated.
- The cluster is looked up by [`cluster_name`](#parameter-cluster-name), so it cannot be renamed with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Spread RDP sessions over two Windows servers
  wallix.bastion.cluster:
    cluster_name: windows-farm
    description: Windows RDS farm
    interactive_logins:
      - srv-win-01:RDP
      - srv-win-02:RDP
    accounts:
      - administrator@local@srv-win-01:RDP
      - administrator@local@srv-win-02:RDP

- name: Replace the interactive logins, keep the accounts
  wallix.bastion.cluster:
    cluster_name: windows-farm
    interactive_logins:
      - srv-win-03:RDP

- name: Remove a cluster
  wallix.bastion.cluster:
    cluster_name: windows-farm
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the cluster already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["interactive_logins"]` |
| <a id="return-cluster"></a>**cluster** | `dict` | The cluster as returned by the Bastion API after the change.<br>In check mode, the expected cluster. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-cluster) |

<a id="sample-cluster"></a>

### Sample of `cluster`

```yaml
account_mappings: []
accounts:
- administrator@local@srv-win-01:RDP
- administrator@local@srv-win-02:RDP
applications: []
cluster_name: windows-farm
description: Windows RDS farm
id: 1a0f769b8c92a15c005056b66c8b
interactive_logins:
- srv-win-01:RDP
- srv-win-02:RDP
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/clusters/1a0f769b8c92a15c005056b66c8b
```
